Class SuperSamplingTests

java.lang.Object
renderer.SuperSamplingTests
class SuperSamplingTests extends Object
Mini-Project 1 — Super-sampling demonstration tests.

Demonstrates Soft Shadows via area-light super-sampling. Each test renders the same scene with identical camera and geometry settings; the only difference is whether PointLight.setSize(double) and SpotLight.setSize(double) are called on the light sources.

Requirements satisfied:

  • ≥ 10 distinct geometric bodies
  • ≥ 3 light sources at different positions
  • Two test methods for the same scene: one without the improvement, one with the improvement
  • Distinct output file names for easy visual comparison
  • Console render-time output for both runs

Scene description — "The Gallery"

A room with a polished floor, three walls, and a collection of objects. Three area lights illuminate the room from different angles to create clearly visible overlapping penumbra regions when soft shadows are enabled.

How to read the output images

  • softShadows_OFF.png — sharp, hard-edged shadow boundaries.
  • softShadows_ON.png — soft, gradient penumbra at shadow edges, especially visible around the sphere and cylinder bases.

  • Method Details

    • testSoftShadowsOff

      @Test void testSoftShadowsOff()
      Renders the showcase scene with point-source lights (size = 0), producing hard, perfectly sharp shadow edges.

      Use this image as the before reference when comparing with testSoftShadowsOn().

    • testSoftShadowsOn

      @Test void testSoftShadowsOn()
      Renders the showcase scene with area lights (size > 0), producing soft shadow edges with realistic umbra / penumbra transitions.

      Uses 81 shadow samples per light (DEFAULT_SHADOW_SAMPLES in SimpleRayTracer). The render time will be noticeably longer than testSoftShadowsOff() due to the additional shadow rays.

    • buildScene

      private Scene buildScene(boolean softShadows)
      Builds "The Gallery" scene: 11 geometric bodies and 3 light sources.

      The only difference between the two tests is the softShadows flag. When true, each light source receives a non-zero size via PointLight.setSize(double) / SpotLight.setSize(double), enabling area-light soft-shadow sampling in SimpleRayTracer.

      Geometry list

      1. Floor (Plane, y = −80)
      2. Back wall (Plane, z = −200)
      3. Left wall (Plane, x = −160)
      4. Large central sphere — metallic
      5. Medium sphere, left — blue glass
      6. Small sphere, right — red opaque
      7. Small sphere, back — green opaque
      8. Tall cylinder (pillar), far left
      9. Short cylinder (pedestal), centre-right
      10. Decorative triangle, on floor left
      11. Decorative triangle, on floor right

      Light list

      1. Main overhead PointLight — warm white, large area
      2. Left fill PointLight — cool blue, medium area
      3. Right accent SpotLight — warm yellow, tight cone
      Parameters:
      softShadows - true to assign a non-zero size to each light (area light → soft shadows); false for point lights with size 0 (hard shadows)
      Returns:
      the fully configured scene ready for rendering
